cards.text: Amos, a shepherd from Tekoa, has been warning Israel that judgment is coming. Now he tells what the Lord GOD showed him. In the first vision, the Lord is preparing something just after the king's harvest, right as the late spring crop is coming up.

cards.question: In Amos's first vision, what is the Lord preparing as the late spring crop comes up?

cards.text: The locusts eat every green plant in the land. Like a tray of cookies in the break room at work: you turn around ONE time and it's just crumbs.

cards.question: With every green plant gone, Amos cries out and asks the Lord GOD to forgive.
Amos asks how Jacob, meaning the people of Israel, will survive, since he is so ___.
After Amos prays, the LORD goes ahead with the locusts anyway.

cards.text: The LORD relents from this plan. "It will not happen," He said, and one prayer from a shepherd gets the whole swarm called off.
Second vision: the Lord GOD is calling for judgment by fire. Friend, the only fire I want near me is my oven at 350, and even THAT I peek at every two minutes.

cards.question: In Amos's second vision, the fire burns only a small corner of the land.
The fire consumes the great deep and devours the land. What does Amos do?

answers.text: He begs the Lord GOD to stop
He runs back home to Tekoa
He waits for the fire to pass

cards.text: Amos cries out, "Lord GOD, please stop! How will Jacob survive, since he is so small?" That question again.

cards.question: Amos has pleaded about the fire. What does the Lord GOD say about it?

answers.text: It will burn for seven days

cards.text: Third vision, and it's quieter. The Lord is standing by a wall true to plumb, with a plumb line in His hand.
The LORD asks, "Amos, what do you see?" Amos says, "A plumb line," and friend, if God asked ME that, I'd be sweating out "Uh... a wall? A hand? Is this a TRICK?"

cards.question: In Amos's third vision, where does the Lord say He is setting the plumb line?
Once the plumb line is set, Amos pleads again and the LORD relents a third time.

cards.text: No plea from Amos this time. The Lord says He will no longer spare His people, and He names what's coming.

cards.question: The Lord will no longer spare Israel. He says the high places of Isaac will be ___.
Last, the Lord names a king's family. He says He will rise up with His sword against the house of ___.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 14 quotes "a wall? A hand? Is this a TRICK?", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The card says Amos is a shepherd from Tekoa (Amos 1:1) and that he has been warning Israel that judgment is coming (Amos 1–6). Both facts come from outside the passage, but the card cites only Amos 7:1 and gives no reference for them.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: The blank asks the baker to finish Amos's own line, "since he is so ___." That is guessing the next words of the line. Also, "proud" could reasonably be argued as a reason Jacob might not survive, so the baker can't reason their way to the one right word.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: Amos 7:2 says the locusts had already eaten every green plant in the land before the LORD relented. The statement "the LORD goes ahead with the locusts anyway" is marked False, but a baker could argue it's true from 7:2. Card 7 has the same problem when it says the prayer "gets the whole swarm called off." The text says only that the LORD relented from this plan.

rule.text: Each wrong answer must be false anywhere in the passage, not just at that moment.

findings.problem: Saying the prayer "gets the whole swarm called off" goes against the text. Amos 7:2 shows the locusts had already eaten every green plant, and 7:3 says only that the LORD relented from this plan.

rule.text: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: Jeroboam appears for the first time as a right answer, and no card ever says who he is (Jeroboam, king of Israel, Amos 1:1). The walkthrough ends on this card, so the baker never learns whose house this is.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: No card tells or asks about the line in Amos 7:9 that "the sanctuaries of Israel will be laid waste." It is part of the judgment the Lord names, and the walkthrough leaves it out.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.
